question: Explain why the wave theory of light fails to account for the existence of threshold frequency in photoelectric emission.

options.A: Wave theory predicts a threshold frequency because energy carried by light depends only on frequency.
options.B: Wave theory associates light energy with intensity, so it would predict that sufficiently intense light of any frequency can eject electrons. Experimentally, no emission occurs below $\nu_0$ even at high intensity; hence it cannot explain threshold frequency.
options.C: Wave theory fails because it predicts the work function to be zero for all metals.
options.D: Wave theory explains threshold frequency by assuming photons have energy $h\nu$.
